messages:
Maria: FYI seeing ~4-6% of TLS handshakes to api.prod in eu-west return the internal fallback cert instead of api.example.com since this morning's ingress rollout. Intermittent across clients.
Lee: Can you paste an s_client capture? Is SNI definitely being sent? :thinking_face:
Maria: added snippet below
Maria: ```
openssl s_client -connect api.prod.eu-west-1.redwood.com:443 -servername api.example.com -alpn h2
CONNECTED(00000003)
Server certificate:
 subject=CN = redwood-internal
 start date: Mar 10 00:00:00 2026 GMT
 issuer: CN = Redwood CA
---
TLS session info: SNI extension present (api.example.com)
```
Devon: SNI present but ALB returned default cert. Could be cert propagation or listener cert ordering. Did we rotate that cert recently?
ingress-bot: deploy event: ingress-controller/eu-west v1.3.0 rolled at 2026-03-16T09:12:40Z by @deploy-bot
Lee: Another possibility: ALB nodes cache cert state; partial propagation during rotation can serve default cert on some edge nodes. Also ALPN/TLS1.3 path differences have bitten us before.
Maria: Correlating IPs — most hits are coming from a partner proxy range behind our NAT (egress-ngw-18). Mobile-ish clients predominately.
Devon: Can you share listener config? Specifically cert ARNs attached and default cert.
Maria: ```
Listener 443 | Default Cert: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:...:redwood-internal
Certificates:
 - arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:...:redwood-internal (default)
 - arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:...:api.example.com
Rules:
 - priority 1: HostHeader api.example.com -> TG-api
 - priority 5: HostHeader example.com -> TG-www
```
Devon: Hmm, I see the api cert is attached but note it lives in eu-west while default is in a different account/region. AWS ALB expects certs to be in same region/account for predictable propagation. Also if the cert was added very recently propagation might be incomplete.
Lee: Can you reproduce with and without -servername and with TLS1.2 vs TLS1.3? I want to see differences in behavior.
Maria: Ran tests. With -servername correct cert ~95% of attempts. Without -servername default cert every time. With -tls1_3 sometimes default even when -servername present.
Maria: ```
# example outputs
with -servername -> CN=api.example.com
with -tls1_3 & -servername -> CN=redwood-internal (in some runs)
```
sre-bot: Runbook reference: edge-tls-debug. Check ACM cert propagation, listener cert count limits, and AWS edge node propagation windows.
Devon: Timeline check — cert was reissued for rotation at 02:00 UTC and ingress-controller rolled new config at ~09:10 UTC. That smells like a rotation + rollout overlap. If the new cert wasn't fully provisioned to all ALB nodes, some nodes could still serve fallback.
Lee: Agreed. Mitigations: 1) gate ingress rollouts until ACM reports cert as "IN USE" across nodes, 2) pre-warm certs by creating them earlier in pipeline, 3) add a probe that verifies per-node cert CN and alerts on mismatch rate.
Maria: I implemented a quick probe script hitting a subset of ALB IPs with -servername and reporting mismatches to our metrics backend. Deployed a temporary rollback of ingress-controller to v1.2.9 in eu-west to stop churn.
deploy-bot: rollback started for ingress-controller/eu-west by @Maria at 2026-03-16T10:01:12Z
Maria: After rollback the fallback cert rate dropped to ~0.6% within 5 minutes. Keeping rollback while we add proper gating/probes.
Devon: Long term: update cert rotation pipeline to include a propagation-wait step and make the gate automatic. Also add visibility in Console: per-listener cert mismatch timeline and percent of nodes serving fallback.
Lee: Add note in runbook about TLS1.3/ALPN weirdness on older edge nodes — call it out as a known edge-case and include mitigation steps.
Maria: Filed INFRA-8592: "ALB cert propagation probe + rotation gating" and assigned to @Devon. I'll add probe design and expected rollout timeline.
Devon: I'll own the automation changes. Also let's add a temporary alert: if >1% of TLS handshakes in a region return CN != expected for 3m, page on-call.
Lee: Good. Also check partner proxy behavior — some proxies reuse connections or manipulate TLS in ways that create odd SNI/ALPN combos. Noted for investigation.
Maria: Thanks everyone — keeping the rollback while we instrument. Will post updates to the ticket and here.
